Hi all — attaching a small spreadsheet (token_calculation_example.xlsx) with two worked examples from April and the general rules used. TL;DR and key points below:

1) Quantum & rounding policy (how we get from raw tokens to invoiceable units) - Streaming or non-streaming requests are metered at token-level internally. For billing, we apply a per-request quantum of 50 tokens for hosted customers by default. That means each request's billed unit is ceil(raw_tokens / 50) * 50.

2) Session amortization (when multiple requests are grouped) - For chat/session workloads using persistent session IDs, we amortize the cost of repeated prefix/context tokens across requests in the same active session window. We define an "active session" as consecutive requests from the same session id with less than 20 minutes idle time. When amortization applies, we bill the first request's full context cost and subsequent requests only for incremental tokens (new prompt + newly generated tokens), still rounded per-request by the 50-token quantum.

3) Long-context surcharge vs KV cache instantiation - The "long context surcharge" label appears when a request causes the runtime to load a larger context window (16k or 32k model variant). That surcharge is applied per request that requires those larger memory paths. If your client keeps using the same session and the KV cache stays warm, subsequent requests that reuse the same cached prefix do not incur the full long-context load again — they are billed only for incremental tokens. However, if the session expires and a new session is instantiated, the first request that re-creates the larger KV cache will again include the longer-context overhead.

Worked example highlights in the spreadsheet:
- Short call (Request A): prompt 120 tokens, model generated 40 tokens -> raw tokens 160 -> ceil(160/50)*50 = 200 billed tokens.
- Long-context call (Request B): prompt 8,200 tokens (historical notes + attachments parsed to 6,000 tokens after compression) + 400 generated tokens -> raw tokens 8,600. Since this crossed your 8k threshold for the 16k model path, the request triggered longer-context memory mapping. We bill that full request as ceil(8600/50)*50 = 8,600 rounded to next 50 => 8,600 (already multiple), and the line shows the surcharge mapping. If subsequent calls within the same session reference the same prefix, they are charged only for the incremental prompt/generation tokens (rounded per request).

4) Microburst smoothing and pilot concessions - For customers with bursty workloads, we can apply a smoothing pilot that reduces per-request rounding impact by aggregating requests into 5-minute micro-windows for billing only for pilot length. That's a contractual opt-in and is shown as a credit line on the invoice when enabled.

I've noted the two invoice line timestamps you mentioned in the spreadsheet. Let us know if you want us to re-run the example with 100-token quantum (we can show both) — some enterprise contracts set a 100-token quantum instead of 50.

Attachment: token_calculation_example.xlsx

Thanks,
